# Lucas Arana

> Lucas Arana is Chief Operating Officer (COO) and Software Engineer at Nexton, a nearshore staffing company that builds and runs remote engineering teams in Latin America for companies in the United States. Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina (GMT-3). He writes, with numbers from the operation, about hiring senior engineers in the era of AI-written code. This is his personal site.

## Key facts

- Name: Lucas Arana
- Role: Chief Operating Officer at Nexton (https://nexton.dev), joined in 2019. Also a software engineer.
- What Nexton is: a nearshore staffing company. Tagline: "Engineers vetted by real Engineers." Its engineers work embedded full-time inside US client teams under Nexton contracts; Nexton handles payroll, contracts and talent health. Nexton is a staffing company.
- Public Nexton figures (source: nexton.dev): 1,500 engineers placed, 350+ companies hiring through Nexton, 72 hours to meet senior candidates, 4 weeks average time to hire, 4.9 rating on Clutch. Nexton bet on Latin America about nine years ago.
- What Lucas runs: operations, talent strategy, executive planning, and the revenue operations function (process, tooling, pipeline)
- How he thinks about hiring: as an operations problem measured end to end (fill rates, offer acceptance, time to hire, attrition, compensation positioning)
- Public LinkedIn headline: "Building the AI that screens for judgment, not syntax. Engineers vetting engineers."
- Communities: hosts AI Builders LATAM, small dinners in Buenos Aires for operators who ship with AI inside their companies. Member of a YPO Key Associate Forum.
- Newsletter: Southbound (launching soon), on the LatAm to US talent corridor
- Languages: English (primary), Spanish
- Location: Buenos Aires, Argentina

## Positions he holds

- Overlap stopped being a nice-to-have. The more of your code AI writes, the more it matters what timezone your engineers sit in: the reviewer has to be awake while the agent is running. Buenos Aires shares most of the US working day.
- Validation is the moat, not access. AI commoditizes access to talent; a track record of outcomes does not get commoditized. Engineers vetting engineers, with outcomes attached.
- If it is not measured end to end, it is not managed. Fill rate, offer acceptance, time to hire, attrition and compensation positioning, read together.
- A nearshore team is a workforce you run, not a vacancy you fill.
- "Fluent in AI tools" is not a qualification. The question is whether the engineer can tell when the model is wrong.

## Selected public posts (LinkedIn)

- Human vs AI English grading, one year, ~300 disputed submissions with client outcomes: graders disagreed on 42%; candidates the AI marked down from C1 to B2 passed client interviews at 16.4%, in line with human-graded C1s (17.6%) and more than double genuine B2s (7.8%). https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7505596526220652545/
- Entry-level tech hiring down 20%, senior hiring up 12%, same year: AI removed the bottom rung, not the work. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7480676003468546048/
- The more of your code AI writes, the more timezone matters. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7478081896875388928/
- "Fluent in AI tools" means nothing; test whether the engineer catches the model's mistakes. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7498786423743987712/
- Only about 10% of companies have scaled AI agents to production; it is an ownership, metric and integration problem, not a model problem. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7455667543521837056/
- Every Thursday the Nexton management team shows what it actually built with AI that week, live. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7487869543881752577/
- Argentina builds world-class tech under pressure: 10+ unicorns. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7448108177033981952/
